title: Microsoft Edge: expanded enforcement controls for Data Loss Prevention connectors
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned expansion from the connector policy fields Microsoft already documents. The roadmap facts, policy fields, prerequisites and configuration routes are supported; the connector landing-page route could include the remaining steps to choose browser actions.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to expand existing Edge for Business DLP Enterprise Connector capabilities.
claims.quote: Microsoft Edge for Business is expanding its existing Data Loss Prevention Enterprise Connector capabilities.

claims.claim: The planned expansion provides more consistent enforcement across download, upload, paste and print workflows.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to configure more consistent enforcement across download, upload, paste, and print workflows.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure and Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: An enabled connector sends content from selected user actions to an on-device DLP agent.
claims.quote: When enabled, Microsoft Edge sends content from specific user actions to the on-device agent and waits for the verdict before proceeding.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Edge for Business natively enforces DLP verdicts from on-device agents.
claims.quote: Microsoft Edge for Business Data Loss Prevention Connectors enable Microsoft Edge for Business to natively enforce DLP (Data Loss Prevention) verdicts from on-device agents.

claims.claim: Setting block_until_verdict to 1 makes Edge wait for the analysis response before giving the page access to the data.
claims.quote: If set to 1, Microsoft Edge waits for a response from the analysis service before giving the page access to the data.

claims.claim: Any other integer value of block_until_verdict allows immediate page access to the data.
claims.quote: Any other integer value allows the page to access the data immediately.

claims.claim: Setting default_action to block denies page access when contacting the analysis service fails.
claims.quote: If set to block, Microsoft Edge denies page access to the data if an error occurs while contacting the analysis service.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A non-block default_action value, including allow, permits page access after an analysis-service communication error.
claims.quote: default_action If set to block, Microsoft Edge denies page access to the data if an error occurs while contacting the analysis service. Any other value permits the page to access the data.

claims.claim: Symantec recommends allow as the configured default_action value.
claims.quote: Configure the following fields in the policy with the recommended values from Symantec: default_action | allow

claims.claim: The connector setup lets administrators choose Allow file access or Block file access for the fallback verdict.
claims.quote: Choose to 'Allow file access' or 'Block file access'. This determines the default verdict if a communication error between Edge and the DLP agent occurs.

claims.claim: Existing connectors require configuration to take effect.
claims.quote: This policy requires further setup to take effect.

claims.where: Scope: Not the same as Purview browser DLP
claims.claim: Edge for Business also enforces Microsoft Purview DLP policies inline in the browser.
claims.quote: Edge for Business enforces Purview DLP policies inline directly in browser, empowering organizations to safeguard sensitive data in real time.

claims.claim: Purview inline browser DLP is a separate configuration route from these third-party agent connectors.
claims.quote: Enable data loss prevention for browser actions: Select the user actions you want to be scanned by Symantec's DLP agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Microsoft Edge > Connectors reaches the page listing connector configurations.
claims.quote: In the main left navigation bar, go to Settings > Microsoft Edge. Navigate to the Connectors tab.
claims.fix: For the Symantec example, give the remaining route in controls[0].note: 'Settings > Microsoft Edge > Connectors > Discover Connectors > Symantec DLP Connector > Set up > Chosen policy > Enable data loss prevention for browser actions'. The setup and action-selection steps are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-connectors-symantec.

claims.claim: OnFileAttachedEnterpriseConnector can be configured through Group Policy or registry using service_provider, enable and disable for the upload action.

claims.claim: A configuration policy must exist before assigning a connector configuration.

claims.claim: The upload policy's block_until_verdict and default_action fields configure verdict waiting and the fallback through Group Policy or registry.

claims.claim: Group Policy Editor > Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Configuration policy for bulk data entry for Microsoft Edge for Business Data Loss Prevention Connectors reaches the policy holding custom guidance.

claims.claim: The custom_messages field in OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector configures guidance through Group Policy or registry.
claims.quote: custom_messages Provides administrator guidance for non-clean analysis results. Value name: OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector

claims.claim: The Edge Management Service connector configuration can be assigned tenant-wide through its configuration policy.
claims.quote: You may also choose to assign this configuration policy to all users in your tenant by selecting Add all users.
